summary: Cathead Mountain fire lookout in Hamilton County, NY: wooden tower 1910, steel LL25 tower 1916, closed 1989; still standing, off limits to the public, reached by helicopter.

facts.design: Aermotor LL25 steel tower erected 1916, with interior stairs added in 1929
facts.status_note: Standing; a radio frame was added over the old tower. Fire lookout service ended after the 1988 season.
facts.agency: New York State Conservation Commission, later the Conservation Department (earlier the Forest, Fish and Game Commission)

access.note: Off limits to the public for many years (per a 2020 newsletter). Summit is privately owned; state land around it bars motor vehicles; equipment is serviced by helicopter.

visit.trail_note: Summit was closed to visitors per the 2020 newsletter (current access unverified) and is privately owned; not a tower to climb

events.note: Wooden lookout tower set up by the Forest, Fish and Game Commission; 15 ft per the annual report quoted by Forest Lookouts, 18 ft per Wikipedia
Observer Edward Smith of Benson named for the Cathead Mountain station in an August 1911 announcement
Steel tower erected, replacing the wooden tower used since 1910; Wikipedia gives 50 ft (15 m) Aermotor LL25
Interior stairs added to the LL25 tower
Tower in service through the end of the 1988 season
Officially closed as a fire lookout in early 1989, after a dispute between a landowner and the state

corrections.why: 4.6 m (15 ft) is the height of the 1910 wooden tower quoted by Forest Lookouts. The 1916 steel tower that stands today is given as 50 ft (15 m) by Wikipedia.

corrections.proposed: New York State Conservation Commission, later the Conservation Department
corrections.why: The brief's agency field holds a fragment of a date line from the Forest Lookouts page. The page names the Conservation Commission and the Conservation Department.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Brief's standing status is confirmed by the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and the 2020 newsletter. Fire lookout service ended in 1988-89, recorded in status_note.

The Forest Lookouts page names observer Edward Smith in a 1911 announcement; a 1954 obituary calls Seth Jack Wadsworth the first to serve in the state's tower. The sources do not agree on who was first, and both are recorded without choosing.
Forest Lookouts quotes a 15-foot tower and Wikipedia gives 18 feet (5.5 m). Not settled. The 15 m figure in facts refers to the 1916 steel tower, not the 1910 tower.

notes_for_editor: Height 15 m comes from Wikipedia, which cites the NYSFFLA searchable list (not read); verify against that list before publishing. The 2020 newsletter is the source for 'off limits'; current access in 2026 is not verified. The Adirondack Explorer article is undated in the copy we read; it refers to 2022 legislation, so it was probably written in 2022 or later, and no later status report was found. The Adirondack Council release (search snippet only) argues a tower can be built without an amendment; not used.
